# Wrist Vehicle Bridge Frontend

## Stack

Next.js 16.2.6 App Router, React 19.2.4, TypeScript 5, npm/package-lock.
Auth.js v5 beta with Google provider, Zod 4 for backend response validation.
Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn-style UI primitives, next-themes, lucide-react.

## Architecture

Single Next.js application with App Router entrypoints in `src/app/` and feature modules in `src/features/`.
Server-only backend clients live under `src/features/*/server/`; client UI and browser APIs live under `components/` and `public/sw.js`.

## Critical Rules

- Before writing Next.js code, read the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/`; this Next version has breaking changes.
- NEVER expose `TESLA_CLIENT_API_TOKEN` to client code, props, service workers, logs, or browser storage.
- Keep `Authorization: Bearer ...` usage only in server-only backend clients protected by `import "server-only"`.
- Use `cache: "no-store"` for authenticated backend fetches that read vehicle, auth, push, or dashboard data.
- Service worker caching is static-only; NEVER cache `/api/`, auth, vehicle, push, dashboard, or navigation responses.
- Server actions that mutate/read private backend data MUST require an authenticated session first.
- Validate backend payloads with strict Zod schemas before trusting data in UI.
- Sensitive vehicle commands (`unlock`, `openFrunk`, `openTrunk`) require explicit client confirmation before execution.
- Do not run `npm run build` unless the user explicitly asks; use lightweight checks such as `npm run lint`.
